title: Example 20-19: Freestanding Stress Marks within Text

illustrates.quote: Follow print when a diacritic symbol is shown in print without an associated letter or word, as in a dictionary entry or instructional material.

blocks.text: The primary stress mark is ′ and the secondary stress mark is ′.
blocks.features: Two freestanding stress marks in running text: the first (primary) is heavier, the second (secondary) is lighter; both sit at the same height in the print image

print.notes: Print original is the picture in the example box; transcribed from the page image (gold-20-A/page-545.png).

braille.notes: Margin stripped: 9. 4 blank source lines between the caption and the first braille line are the print-original picture area, not braille, and are excluded.

uncertain: The two freestanding marks print alike (same height); the braille's high (^.b) and low (^.24) forms cannot be derived from the print.
resolution: braille.lines: A and B agree on every character; they differ only in that B also lists the 4 blank source lines after the caption as braille lines (leading '' entries). Those lines are the print-original picture area (page image shows the print text there), so they are excluded here; A's version is kept. illustrates: A recorded rule '20.x' and the file title as the quote (not the rule's wording); B's rule id was usable but its quote was sometimes a spliced page footer or a table-of-contents line. printCorrections.was: Freestanding stress marks shown as prime marks in the image (primary high, secondary lower per the braille)
printCorrections.now: Two freestanding stress marks: first heavier, second lighter, both at the same height
printCorrections.evidence: references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf p.545, rendered at 300 dpi and cropped to the Example 20-19 box: the two marks after "is" are both drawn at the top of the line; they differ in weight, not in height. The old wording took "secondary lower" from the braille, not from the print. The text field (U+02C8 / U+02CC) is left unchanged: the image does not settle which Unicode characters the two glyphs are (cannot settle), so the runner result is unaffected.

printCorrections.was: "...primary stress mark is ˈ and the secondary stress mark is ˌ." (U+02C8 high mark, U+02CC low mark)
printCorrections.now: "...primary stress mark is ′ and the secondary stress mark is ′." (the same prime, U+2032, twice)
printCorrections.evidence: references/_gemini/gold-20-A/page-545.png (Example 20-19 box): both freestanding marks are drawn at the same height, one slightly heavier; the high/low distinction (braille ^.b versus ^.24) exists only in the braille lines. The text field had used a high and a low mark, which is that braille distinction read back into the print. Because the print marks are alike, the input carries no such distinction.
